Remarks

PhysicsObject extends GameObject with velocity, mass, drag, constant acceleration, and per-frame accumulated force, acceleration, and impulse inputs.

The simulation step is intentionally simple and game-friendly: accumulated impulses are applied directly to velocity, accumulated force inputs are converted to acceleration, accumulated acceleration inputs are applied directly, drag is applied, and then position is advanced using the resulting velocity.

A mass less than or equal to zero is treated as 1 for force and impulse conversion.

In this class, force is mass-dependent input that is converted to acceleration during the physics step, acceleration is mass-independent input that is applied directly to velocity over time, and impulse is an immediate velocity change that is applied before acceleration and drag for the current step. Use AddForce(Vector2) for force-like input, AddAcceleration(Vector2) for direct acceleration input, and AddImpulse(Vector2) for one-shot impacts, jumps, knockback, or collision responses.

Properties

AccumulatedAcceleration

Gets the accumulated acceleration contribution to be applied on the next update.

public Vector2 AccumulatedAcceleration { get; }

Property Value

Vector2

Remarks

This member stores acceleration input directly, without any mass conversion. Calling AddAcceleration(Vector2) changes AccumulatedAcceleration.

AccumulatedForce

Gets the accumulated force input to be applied on the next update.

public Vector2 AccumulatedForce { get; }

Property Value

Vector2

Remarks

This member stores force-like input in engine units. It is converted to acceleration during the physics step by dividing it by the effective mass. Calling AddForce(Vector2) changes AccumulatedForce.

AccumulatedImpulses

Gets the accumulated impulses to be applied on the next update.

public Vector2 AccumulatedImpulses { get; }

Property Value

Vector2

Remarks

Calling AddImpulse(Vector2) changes AccumulatedImpulses. AccumulatedImpulses stores the velocity delta that will be added during the next physics step. Use this for one-time impulses, not for constant acceleration.

ConstAcceleration

Gets or sets the constant acceleration applied every update (e.g., gravity).
